title: The impact of transurethral en bloc resection on the dissemination of circulating tumor cells and tumor DNA in NMIBC compared with conventional TUR-B
summary: In patients with non–muscle-invasive bladder cancer, the tumor is usually removed through the urethra. In the conventional method (TUR-B), the tumor is often removed in multiple pieces. This may allow tumor cells to enter the bloodstream. Circulating tumor cells or fragments of tumor DNA in the blood can indicate a potential spread of the disease. An alternative surgical method is the en-bloc resection, in which the tumor is removed in a single piece. This may reduce the release of tumor cells during surgery and could potentially improve prognosis. This study investigates whether the method of tumor removal affects the levels of circulating tumor cells and tumor DNA in the blood. Three surgical techniques are compared: en-bloc resection with prior injection of a fluid cushion under the tumor (hydrodissection), en-bloc resection with a laser, and conventional resection of the bladder tumor using an electric loop (TUR-B). A total of 69 patients will be enrolled, with 23 in each group. Blood and urine samples will be collected before, during, and up to 12 hours after surgery. In addition, a laboratory cell model will be created from tumor tissue to allow further study of the tumor. Follow-up cystoscopies will be performed at three and twelve months after surgery.

interventions.name:
Surgical resection of bladder tumor:
Transurethral resection of bladder tumor using an electrocautery loop (TUR-B)

Surgical resection of bladder tumor:
Transurethral en bloc resection of bladder tumor (TUeb) using a thulium laser

Surgical resection of bladder tumor:
Transurethral en bloc resection of bladder tumor (TUEB) using the HybridKnife with hydrodissection of tissue layers (HydroJet)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Provision of written informed consent after patient education
Age ≥ 18 years
Cystoscopically confirmed bladder tumor (initial diagnosis or recurrence)
Tumor size ≤ 6 cm
Exclusion criteria:
Any circumstances that make study participation undesirable for the subjects
No written informed consent provided
Bladder tumor ≤ 5 mm
≥ 5 malignant‑suspected intravesical lesions
Intravesical instillation therapy within the last 8 weeks
Muscle‑invasive bladder tumor
Presence of metastasis
Bladder tumor too large to be resected en bloc
Patients unable to provide consent
Benign histological finding
